$doc: Vyomi capability registry — DynamoDB. See s3.json for the contract.

dynamodb.table.crud.title: Tables (create, describe, list, delete)
limitations: Table names shorter than 3 characters are accepted (DynamoDB requires 3-255).

CreateTable with neither BillingMode nor ProvisionedThroughput creates an on-demand table; DynamoDB defaults to PROVISIONED and rejects the request with "No provisioned throughput specified for the table".
New tables and indexes are ACTIVE immediately (no CREATING phase on DescribeTable).

dynamodb.item.crud.title: Items (put, get, update, delete, query, scan, batch, transactions)
limitations: Differential parity vs DynamoDB Local (tests/parity/ddb_differential.py, report in tests/parity/reports/): 149 of 152 hand-written cases (658 of 661 responses) and 400 of 400 random 30-operation sequences match; the 3 deviating cases are the TTL and CreateTable leniencies documented in this file.
Scan returns items in key order, not DynamoDB's storage-hash order, so Scan page boundaries and Segment membership differ (the union of all pages/segments is identical).
The 1 MB page limit is not applied to Query/Scan, and BatchGetItem/BatchWriteItem never return Unprocessed keys/items.
ConsumedCapacity is not reported (ReturnConsumedCapacity is ignored) and capacity is never throttled.
TransactWriteItems ClientRequestToken idempotency is not tracked.
Maximum nesting depth (32) of maps/lists is not enforced.

dynamodb.table.settings.title: Table class, deletion protection, encryption (at create)
limitations: Deletion protection is enforced (DeleteTable is rejected while it is on).
Table class and encryption at rest are stored and returned but have no effect; data is not encrypted at rest.

dynamodb.table.update.title: Update capacity / settings (UpdateTable)
limitations: Provisioned capacity is recorded but not enforced — Vyomi never throttles requests.

dynamodb.table.ttl.title: Time to Live (TTL)
limitations: Expired items are removed when they are read, queried or scanned — not by a background process within ~48 hours as in AWS.

dynamodb.table.pitr.title: Point-in-time recovery (PITR)
limitations: RestoreTableToPointInTime is enforced against the PITR window (rejected without PITR enabled, or for a RestoreDateTime outside [EarliestRestorableDateTime, LatestRestorableDateTime]) but always restores the table's current state — Vyomi keeps no change history, so every point in the window yields the same (latest) data.

dynamodb.partiql.title: PartiQL editor
limitations: Supported: SELECT (projection, WHERE with = <> < <= > >= BETWEEN IN AND/OR/NOT begins_with contains attribute_type size IS [NOT] MISSING, ? parameters, "table"."index"), INSERT ... VALUE (maps, lists, <<sets>>), UPDATE ... SET/REMOVE ... WHERE <full key> [AND condition], DELETE FROM ... WHERE <full key>.
Not supported: BatchExecuteStatement, ExecuteTransaction, NextToken paging, arithmetic in UPDATE SET.
